name: Melat Kiros
bio: Melat Kiros is a lawyer and public affairs PhD student at the University of Colorado Denver who was born in Ethiopia and grew up in Aurora, Colorado. She holds degrees from Washington College and Notre Dame Law School and worked as a securities regulatory associate at Sidley Austin. A democratic socialist, she defeated incumbent Diana DeGette in the June 2026 Democratic primary.

platform.point: Enact Medicare for All, cancel medical debt and cap prescription drug prices.
Pursue a Housing First approach with upzoning, permitting reform, federal rent control and social housing.
Move toward universal childcare, capping costs at 10% of family income and free care for low-income families.
Impose a full arms embargo on Israel, reassert congressional war powers and cut Pentagon spending by 10%.
Raise the federal minimum wage to a $15 floor adjusted for local costs and raise taxes on the ultra-wealthy.
Pass a Green New Deal focused on public transit, and pause data center construction until federal rules exist.

economy.evidence: Supports higher taxes on the ultra-wealthy, federal rent control, drug-price caps and a higher local-cost minimum wage.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All, medical debt cancellation and universal childcare.

immigration.evidence: Supports abolishing ICE and releasing detainees without criminal records, alongside more immigration judges.

foreign.evidence: Supports an arms embargo on Israel, opposes military action against Iran and backs a 10% Pentagon cut.

energy.evidence: Supports a Green New Deal centered on public transit and walkable neighborhoods.

tech.evidence: Supports a moratorium on data centers until federal labor and environmental regulations are in place.

notes: No public positions found on abortion, guns, LGBTQ rights, policing, education or religion, so those domains are unscored. The Commons portrait relies on an unverified emailed permission from a 2026 event photographer, so it was not used.

name: Joe Neguse
bio: Joe Neguse has represented Colorado's 2nd District since 2019 and has served as House Assistant Democratic Leader since 2024. He was previously a University of Colorado Regent and executive director of the Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies. Born in Bakersfield, California, to Eritrean immigrant parents, he is a graduate of the University of Colorado Boulder and its law school.

platform.point: Ban stock trading by members of Congress and clean up government.
Protect Colorado's public lands and block efforts to sell them off.
Lead House Democrats' litigation task force challenging obstruction of congressional oversight.
Advance climate action, forest management and wildfire mitigation legislation.
Strengthen antitrust enforcement in digital markets and scrutinize pharmaceutical mergers.

economy.evidence: Opposed the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and universal health coverage.

liberty.evidence: Pro-choice on abortion, backs the Equality Act and national cannabis legalization, and supports universal background checks for guns.

security.evidence: Sponsored stricter police accountability rules and supports police reform.

immigration.evidence: Supports a pathway to citizenship and the DREAM Act and opposed using troops at the southern border.

energy.evidence: Calls climate change an existential threat and supports the Green New Deal and renewable incentives.

tech.evidence: As antitrust subcommittee vice chair, backs stronger enforcement against anticompetitive digital market practices and sponsored net neutrality legislation.

notes: Campaign website could not be confirmed, so official House accounts are listed.

name: Jeff Hurd
bio: Jeff Hurd has represented Colorado's 3rd District since January 2025 and chairs the Natural Resources Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs. A lawyer from Grand Junction, he clerked for a federal appeals judge and founded his own law firm. He is a member of the Republican Governance Group.

platform.point: Secure the border by resourcing Border Patrol and law enforcement cooperation while supporting legal immigration.
Bring higher-paying jobs to rural Colorado and remove unnecessary regulations on small businesses.
Ease family costs through job creation and tools such as the Child Tax Credit and childcare assistance.
Develop Colorado's oil, gas and renewable resources, pursue energy independence and reform permitting.
Protect upstream Colorado water interests and support farmers and ranchers through the Farm Bill.
Support blockchain and crypto innovation with sensible rules such as the FIT21 bill.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on removing unnecessary regulations, though he voted to rescind tariffs on Canada.

welfare.evidence: Joined moderate Republicans refusing to back a reconciliation bill cutting Medicaid for vulnerable people and supports the Child Tax Credit.

immigration.evidence: Prioritizes border security and more Border Patrol resources while supporting legal immigration.

energy.evidence: Supports developing oil and natural gas alongside renewables, energy independence and permitting reform.

tech.evidence: Backs the FIT21 crypto market structure bill and a light-touch approach to blockchain regulation.

notes: The campaign site image found was a logo rather than a headshot.

name: Dwayne Romero
bio: Dwayne Romero is a U.S. Army engineer officer, combat veteran and small-business owner running as the Democratic nominee for Colorado's 3rd District. He has served as a school board president, city council member and Colorado economic development director, and sits on a local water and sanitation district board.

platform.point: Repeal tariffs and expand family tax credits to help households afford basics.
Keep rural hospitals funded, let Medicare negotiate drug prices and protect reproductive care.
Make protecting Colorado's water a top job and resist efforts to pull water from the basin.
Oppose selling public lands and fund wildfire fighting and resilience.
Pair border security with citizenship pathways for long-term residents and more immigration judges.
Ban congressional stock trading, end dark money, adopt term limits and close the lobbying revolving door.

economy.evidence: Wants tariffs repealed, family tax credits expanded and corporate home purchases restricted.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Medicaid and SNAP reductions, backs Medicare drug price negotiation and rural hospital funding.

liberty.evidence: Supports protecting access to reproductive health care (abortion); no stated positions on other liberty issues.

immigration.evidence: Supports border security together with a pathway to citizenship for long-term residents.

energy.evidence: Backs an all-of-the-above approach using legacy energy while expanding alternative energy.

notes: Campaign social links are site redirects that could not be resolved to full account URLs; no Wikipedia article or Commons photo found.
